## Purpose

Fixes #49250.

When a synchronous external KV load is rejected under
`kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"`, scheduler state is rewound but Model
Runner V2 can retain state written by discarded in-flight frames. With
overlapping batches, the stale state can affect later decoding. The result does
not match full recomputation.

This change:

- marks the exact in-flight token positions stale and clears speculative and
  placeholder state when a failed load is recomputed;
- derives the safe shared-prefix offset from all active optimistic frames while
  excluding output that was already marked stale;
- serializes repair of physically shared KV blocks: dependent requests wait for
  worker-confirmed owner progress (or a safely ordered Model Runner V2
  same-frame repair), invalid blocks are quarantined from new prefix-cache
  users, and unfinished repair ownership transfers on cancellation/preemption;
- propagates an explicit `rewound_req_ids` marker with cached-request data;
- applies the scheduler's absolute computed-token offset to Model Runner V2
  only for those explicit rollbacks;
- restores device-side token history, sequence length, last sampled token, and
  output penalty counts to the scheduler's accepted output prefix;
- clears speculative draft/lookahead state and resets sampled-history caches;
- restores Mamba hybrid acceptance and align-copy state from the same absolute
  scheduler position; and
- adds focused scheduler and worker regression tests, including a multi-token
  speculative async frame and emulated rank-local/PP ordering.

There is no connector-specific special case.

This is materially different from #49252. That PR's scheduler fix derives a
frame count from `num_output_placeholders - 1` and explicitly scopes out
speculative decoding and diffusion. This change uses the existing exact
`num_in_flight_tokens` accounting and an explicit CPU-to-GPU rewind signal; it
was validated with EAGLE3. The difference was documented on #49250 before this
PR was opened.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_output_aggregator.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_kv_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files <changed-files>

git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
```

GPU negative-control protocol:

1. Run greedy decoding without a KV connector and record token IDs.
2. Use a connector that promises a block-aligned synchronous load and rejects
   it before copying KV.
3. Compare clean-base and patched output against the no-connector baseline for
   sync, async, and async EAGLE3 scheduling.
4. Repeat with real `LMCacheConnectorV1`, injecting a one-shot failure in a
   16-token retrieval before KV is copied.

The Codex-review follow-ups add direct device-state controls. One simulates two
discarded sampled tokens and compares exact old head `b688039af0` with the
patched worker. The other restores Mamba align state at absolute offsets 0, 8,
and 9 while preserving unrelated request slots.

## Test Result

Rebase validation at `22fdd4d9be`, on `main` base `eed1f3d0c6` (2026-09-12):

- **330 tests passed**: 118 recovery/worker/Mamba/sampling tests on the RTX
  5060 Ti, 208 CPU scheduler/connector compatibility tests, and 4 upstream
  block-table tests. Applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.
- The `update_requests()` conflict resolution retains both upstream's
  authoritative `block_table_updates` and the PR's state rewind. A combined
  regression checks replacement without duplicate appends, ordinary appends
  for other requests, and accepted-state rollback. Retaining the pre-rebase
  method fails the replacement case as intended; the resolved code passes.
- Ten cold GPU cells completed. OPT-125M recovery matched all eight baseline
  tokens, with one rejected 16-token block and zero copied bytes. Qwen
  owner/dependent ordering passed at threshold 32 (sync/async) and 64 (sync).
- All token outputs and producer KV match the sealed `e6aca2d6ae` runs, with
  matching model revisions and runtime identities. This is comparison against
  retained prior evidence, not a fresh old-head rerun.
- The threshold-64 exact dual oracle remains **3/4**: both rejected requests
  match clean recomputation, while unaffected request 4 differs from reuse.
  The previous same-runtime old-head controls and logit traces localized this
  pre-existing difference to a BF16 tie (recovery: 16.25/16.25; reuse margin:
  0.125). It remains an exact-output limitation, not an all-output pass.
- Threshold-32 full-output differences are also unchanged; the affected
  shared peer matches clean recomputation in both scheduler modes. Ordering
  safety and exact-output equality remain separate checks.

Earlier `ff850131de` negative controls exposed premature dependent scheduling,
adoption of quarantined blocks, and missing owner transfer after cancellation.
The shared-block fix at `f2e2abd460` passed the ordering invariant in all four
earlier threshold-32 paired runs.

The Qwen follow-up compares rejected requests against connector-free full
recomputation and unaffected requests against successful reuse, while checking
state and ordering invariants separately. Different execution shapes can
change BF16 rounding and greedy near-tie outcomes, so whole-file comparison
with the successful external-load baseline is insufficient on its own.

Guanxin Li independently repeated this dual-oracle check on a GH200 at exact
head `f2e2abd460`: both rejected requests matched full recomputation and both
unaffected requests matched successful reuse. This also corrected the earlier
interpretation of an `819f20e19f` whole-file mismatch; that mismatch compared
different valid execution paths rather than showing recovery corruption.

Full all-request byte equality can still vary at BF16
ties/near-ties when the execution shape changes. Exact logit traces and an
unrelated-request control separate that numerical sensitivity from the
owner/dependent scheduling invariant fixed here.

Codex-review device-state control on NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti:

| State after rewind | `b688039af0` | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| `total_len` | stale: 5 | restored: 3 |
| last sampled token | stale: 21 | restored: 10 |
| discarded token counts | 1, 1 | 0, 0 |
| draft/lookahead state | stale | cleared |

The Triton rewind passed with and without output penalty counts. The Mamba CUDA
regression passed for zero, boundary, and boundary-plus-one offsets; its exact
base negative control failed because model-state rewind was absent.

Earlier single-GPU negative controls (NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, Model Runner V2
asserted, greedy token-ID comparison):

| Configuration | Clean base | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Controlled rejection, sync | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Controlled rejection, async | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| EAGLE3 async, 2 draft tokens | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Real LMCache rejection, sync | differs from scratch | exact |
| Real LMCache rejection, async | differs from scratch | exact |

The later sampled-state E2E prompt is not a negative control for the old head:
both old and patched code happened to choose the same greedy tokens. The direct
old-versus-patched state control isolates that review finding.

Not covered: real multi-GPU/NCCL execution, full-model Mamba/RecoverSSM
load-rejection integration, layerwise connector loading, performance,
partial-copy failure, or cross-hardware bitwise determinism.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation,
implementation, and test orchestration. The human submitter reviewed the
sampled-state, Mamba-state, single-GPU parallel-simulation, and shared-block
ordering follow-ups, and remains responsible for the change.

change BF16 rounding and greedy near-tie outcomes, so whole-file comparison
with the successful external-load baseline is insufficient on its own.

Guanxin Li independently repeated this dual-oracle check on a GH200 at exact
head `f2e2abd460`: both rejected requests matched full recomputation and both
unaffected requests matched successful reuse. This also corrected the earlier
interpretation of an `819f20e19f` whole-file mismatch; that mismatch compared
different valid execution paths rather than showing recovery corruption.

Full all-request byte equality can still vary at BF16
ties/near-ties when the execution shape changes. Exact logit traces and an
unrelated-request control separate that numerical sensitivity from the
owner/dependent scheduling invariant fixed here.

Codex-review device-state control on NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti:

| State after rewind | `b688039af0` | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| `total_len` | stale: 5 | restored: 3 |
| last sampled token | stale: 21 | restored: 10 |
| discarded token counts | 1, 1 | 0, 0 |
| draft/lookahead state | stale | cleared |

The Triton rewind passed with and without output penalty counts. The Mamba CUDA
regression passed for zero, boundary, and boundary-plus-one offsets; its exact
base negative control failed because model-state rewind was absent.

Earlier single-GPU negative controls (NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti, Model Runner V2
asserted, greedy token-ID comparison):

| Configuration | Clean base | Patched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Controlled rejection, sync | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Controlled rejection, async | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| EAGLE3 async, 2 draft tokens | differs from baseline | exact, 2/2 |
| Real LMCache rejection, sync | differs from scratch | exact |
| Real LMCache rejection, async | differs from scratch | exact |

The later sampled-state E2E prompt is not a negative control for the old head:
both old and patched code happened to choose the same greedy tokens. The direct
old-versus-patched state control isolates that review finding.

Not covered: real multi-GPU/NCCL execution, full-model Mamba/RecoverSSM
load-rejection integration, layerwise connector loading, performance,
partial-copy failure, or cross-hardware bitwise determinism.

+    num_common_prefix_blocks = 50
+    num_prompt_tokens = num_prompt_blocks * scheduler.block_size
+    num_external_computed_tokens = num_external_computed_blocks * scheduler.block_size
+    common_prefix_len = num_common_prefix_blocks * scheduler.block_size

+    request1 = create_request(
+        num_tokens=num_prompt_tokens,

+        request2.num_in_flight_tokens
+        > failed_output.num_scheduled_tokens[request2.request_id]
+    )
+    # A shared peer can also have an older frame that was already detached
+    # from num_computed_tokens by a preemption/reset but has not returned yet.
+    # It must not be subtracted a second time while finding the safe prefix.
+    request2.num_computed_tokens -= preexisting_stale_tokens
+    request2.num_stale_output_tokens = preexisting_stale_tokens
+

+    req2_block_ids = failed_output.scheduled_new_reqs[1].block_ids[0]

+    )
+
+    assert request1.num_computed_tokens == 0
+    # request2 relies on request1 to restore the shared invalid block. Its own
+    # safe offset is the confirmed local prefix, excluding every async frame
+    # still in flight when the load failure is reported.
+    assert request2.num_computed_tokens == common_prefix_len
+    assert (
+        request2.num_stale_output_tokens
+        == stale_output.num_scheduled_tokens[request2.request_id]

+def _setup_shared_sync_load_failure(
+    *,
+    async_scheduling: bool = False,
+    aux_output: bool = False,
+    num_sharers: int = 1,
+    invalid_block_idx: int = 0,
+    num_external_computed_blocks: int = 9,
+    num_common_prefix_blocks: int = 4,
+    num_sharer_external_blocks: int = 0,
+    max_num_batched_tokens: int | None = None,
+    long_prefill_token_threshold: int = 32,
+) -> tuple[Scheduler, Request, list[Request]]:
+    """Create a small owner/sharer recovery with a 32-token prefill cap."""
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        max_num_batched_tokens=(
+            max_num_batched_tokens or max(64, 32 * (num_sharers + 1))
+        ),
+        kv_load_failure_policy="recompute",
+    )
+    vllm_config.scheduler_config.async_scheduling = async_scheduling
+    vllm_config.scheduler_config.long_prefill_token_threshold = (
+        long_prefill_token_threshold
+    )
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config)
+    scheduler.use_v2_model_runner = True
+
+    num_prompt_blocks = 10
+    if aux_output:
+        scheduler.aux_output_connector = AuxOutputSchedulerConnector()
+    num_prompt_tokens = num_prompt_blocks * scheduler.block_size
+    num_external_computed_tokens = num_external_computed_blocks * scheduler.block_size
+    common_prefix_len = num_common_prefix_blocks * scheduler.block_size
+
+    owner = create_request(
+        num_tokens=num_prompt_tokens,
+        common_prefix_len=common_prefix_len,
+    )
+    sharers = [
+        create_request(
+            num_tokens=num_prompt_tokens,
+            common_prefix_len=common_prefix_len,
+        )
+        for _ in range(num_sharers)
+    ]
+    scheduler.add_request(owner)
+    for sharer in sharers:
+        scheduler.add_request(sharer)
+
+    scheduler.connector = create_mock_connector()
+    external_matches = {owner.request_id: num_external_computed_tokens}
+    external_matches.update(
+        {
+            sharer.request_id: num_sharer_external_blocks * scheduler.block_size
+            for sharer in sharers
+        }
+    )
+    scheduler.connector.get_num_new_matched_tokens.side_effect = (
+        _make_get_num_new_matched_tokens(
+            external_matches,
+            async_load=False,
+        )
+    )
+    scheduler.connector.request_finished.return_value = (False, None)
+    scheduler.connector.take_events.return_value = ()
+
+    failed_output = scheduler.schedule()
+    owner_block_ids = failed_output.scheduled_new_reqs[0].block_ids[0]
+    for scheduled_sharer in failed_output.scheduled_new_reqs[1:]:
+        assert (
+            scheduled_sharer.block_ids[0][:num_common_prefix_blocks]
+            == owner_block_ids[:num_common_prefix_blocks]
+        )
+
+    scheduler.update_from_output(
+        failed_output,
+        create_model_runner_output(
+            [owner, *sharers],
+            invalid_block_ids={owner_block_ids[invalid_block_idx]},
+        ),
+    )
+
+    invalid_prefix_len = invalid_block_idx * scheduler.block_size
+    assert owner.num_computed_tokens == invalid_prefix_len
+    for sharer in sharers:
+        assert sharer.num_computed_tokens == common_prefix_len
+    return scheduler, owner, sharers
+
+
+def _update_prefill_frame(
+    scheduler: Scheduler,
+    scheduler_output,
+    requests: list[Request],
+) -> None:
+    model_runner_output = create_model_runner_output(requests)
+    model_runner_output.sampled_token_ids = [[] for _ in requests]
+    scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, model_runner_output)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True])
+def test_shared_block_recovery_waits_for_confirmed_owner_progress(
+    async_scheduling: bool,
+):
+    scheduler, owner, (sharer,) = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure(
+        async_scheduling=async_scheduling
+    )
+
+    first_recovery = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert first_recovery.num_scheduled_tokens == {owner.request_id: 32}
+
+    # Async scheduling may enqueue another frame before the first one returns.
+    # Optimistically scheduled owner tokens must not release the sharer.
+    second_recovery = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert second_recovery.num_scheduled_tokens == {owner.request_id: 32}
+
+    _update_prefill_frame(scheduler, first_recovery, [owner])
+    assert owner.num_computed_tokens - owner.num_in_flight_tokens == 32
+
+    _update_prefill_frame(scheduler, second_recovery, [owner])
+    assert owner.num_computed_tokens - owner.num_in_flight_tokens == 64
+
+    released = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert released.num_scheduled_tokens.get(sharer.request_id, 0) > 0
+
+
+def test_shared_block_recovery_waits_all_sharers():
+    scheduler, owner, sharers = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure(num_sharers=3)
+
+    recovery = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert recovery.num_scheduled_tokens == {owner.request_id: 32}
+    assert all(
+        sharer.request_id not in recovery.num_scheduled_tokens for sharer in sharers
+    )
+
+
+def test_shared_block_recovery_allows_ordered_same_frame_release():
+    scheduler, owner, (sharer,) = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure()
+
+    first_owner_frame = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert first_owner_frame.num_scheduled_tokens == {owner.request_id: 32}
+    _update_prefill_frame(scheduler, first_owner_frame, [owner])
+
+    # The owner has 32 confirmed tokens and writes the remaining 32 shared
+    # tokens in this frame. MRV2 writes KV for the whole frame before any
+    # request's attention reads it, so the sharer's private suffix is safe to
+    # schedule in the same frame.
+    boundary_frame = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert boundary_frame.num_scheduled_tokens == {
+        owner.request_id: 32,
+        sharer.request_id: 32,
+    }
+
+
+def test_shared_block_recovery_v1_requires_confirmed_release():
+    scheduler, owner, (sharer,) = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure()
+    scheduler.use_v2_model_runner = False
+
+    first_owner_frame = scheduler.schedule()
+    _update_prefill_frame(scheduler, first_owner_frame, [owner])
+
+    boundary_frame = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert boundary_frame.num_scheduled_tokens == {owner.request_id: 32}
+    _update_prefill_frame(scheduler, boundary_frame, [owner])

+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "threshold,batch_budget,invalid_block_idx",
+    [
+        (1, 32, 0),
+        (15, 32, 0),
+        (16, 32, 0),
+        (17, 32, 0),
+        (31, 32, 0),
+        (32, 32, 0),
+        (33, 64, 0),
+        (64, 64, 0),
+        (1, 64, 3),
+        (15, 64, 3),
+        (16, 64, 3),
+        (17, 64, 3),
+        (31, 64, 3),
+        (32, 64, 3),
+        (33, 96, 3),
+        (64, 96, 3),
+    ],
+)
+def test_shared_block_recovery_scheduling_boundary_matrix(
+    async_scheduling: bool,
+    threshold: int,
+    batch_budget: int,
+    invalid_block_idx: int,
+):
+    scheduler, owner, (sharer,) = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure(
+        async_scheduling=async_scheduling,
+        invalid_block_idx=invalid_block_idx,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=batch_budget,
+        long_prefill_token_threshold=threshold,
+    )
+    required_end = 4 * scheduler.block_size
+
+    for _ in range(required_end + 1):
+        confirmed_before = scheduler._get_confirmed_num_computed_tokens(owner)
+        active_before = owner.num_in_flight_tokens - owner.num_stale_output_tokens
+        owner_offset_before = owner.num_computed_tokens
+        output = scheduler.schedule()
+        owner_scheduled = output.num_scheduled_tokens.get(owner.request_id, 0)
+
+        if sharer.request_id in output.num_scheduled_tokens:
+            ordered_by_confirmed_progress = confirmed_before >= required_end
+            ordered_inside_frame = (
+                active_before == 0
+                and owner_offset_before == confirmed_before
+                and confirmed_before + owner_scheduled >= required_end
+            )
+            assert ordered_by_confirmed_progress or ordered_inside_frame
+            break
+
+        assert owner_scheduled > 0
+        scheduled_requests = [
+            request
+            for request in (owner, sharer)
+            if request.request_id in output.num_scheduled_tokens
+        ]
+        _update_prefill_frame(scheduler, output, scheduled_requests)
+    else:
+        pytest.fail("shared-block recovery dependency did not make progress")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("aux_output", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("sharer_queue", ["running", "kv_holding", "deferred"])
+def test_shared_block_recovery_reassigns_cancelled_owner(
+    aux_output: bool, sharer_queue: str
+):
+    scheduler, owner, (sharer,) = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure(aux_output=aux_output)
+    if sharer_queue != "running":
+        scheduler.running.remove(sharer)
+        sharer.status = RequestStatus.WAITING
+        if sharer_queue == "kv_holding":
+            scheduler._enqueue_waiting_request(sharer)
+        # A skipped peer remains tracked even while schedule() holds it in
+        # a temporary queue. Also cover deduplication of a queued deferred peer.
+        scheduler.deferred_waiting.add(sharer)
+    owner_block_ids = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(owner.request_id)[0]
+    sharer_block_ids = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(sharer.request_id)[0]
+    owner_only_block_id = next(
+        block_id for block_id in owner_block_ids if block_id not in sharer_block_ids
+    )
+    assert (
+        scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool.blocks[owner_only_block_id].block_hash
+        is not None
+    )
+
+    scheduler.finish_requests(owner.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+
+    assert sharer.num_computed_tokens == 0
+    assert not scheduler._kv_recovery_dependencies
+    assert {
+        owner_id for owner_id, _ in scheduler._kv_recovery_block_owners.values()
+    } == {sharer.request_id}
+    assert (
+        scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool.blocks[owner_only_block_id].block_hash
+        is None
+    )
+    if sharer_queue == "deferred":
+        scheduler.kv_holding_waiting.add_request(sharer)
+    recovery = scheduler.schedule()
+    # With no competing request, the prefill cap no longer limits the budget.
+    assert recovery.num_scheduled_tokens == {
+        sharer.request_id: scheduler.max_num_scheduled_tokens
+    }
+    assert sharer not in scheduler.deferred_waiting
+    if aux_output:
+        assert recovery.aux_output_connector_metadata is not None
+        assert recovery.aux_output_connector_metadata.finished_requests == (
+            owner.request_id,
+        )
+
+
+def test_shared_block_recovery_transfers_to_deferred_peer_in_stable_order():
+    scheduler, owner, sharers = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure(num_sharers=2)
+    sharers = sorted(sharers, key=lambda req: req.request_id)
+    for sharer in reversed(sharers):
+        scheduler.running.remove(sharer)
+        sharer.status = RequestStatus.WAITING
+        scheduler.deferred_waiting.add(sharer)
+
+    scheduler.finish_requests(owner.request_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+
+    new_owner, dependent = sharers
+    assert new_owner.num_computed_tokens == 0
+    assert dependent.num_computed_tokens == 4 * scheduler.block_size
+    assert scheduler._kv_recovery_dependencies == {
+        dependent.request_id: {new_owner.request_id: 4 * scheduler.block_size}
+    }
+    # Restore the transient queue with the dependent first: it must stay
+    # deferred while the new owner makes progress behind it.
+    for sharer in reversed(sharers):
+        scheduler.kv_holding_waiting.add_request(sharer)
+    recovery = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert recovery.num_scheduled_tokens == {new_owner.request_id: 32}
+    assert list(scheduler.kv_holding_waiting) == [dependent]
+    assert scheduler.deferred_waiting == {dependent}
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("invalid_block_idx", [0, 2])
+def test_shared_block_recovery_quarantines_prefix_cache_hits(

+        invalid_block_idx=invalid_block_idx,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=96,

+    newcomer_block_ids = scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_block_ids(newcomer.request_id)[

+def test_shared_block_recovery_quarantines_divergent_fallback_hit():
+    scheduler, owner, (sharer,) = _setup_shared_sync_load_failure(
+        invalid_block_idx=2,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=96,
+    )
+    expected_valid_tokens = 2 * scheduler.block_size
+
+    newcomer = create_request(
+        num_tokens=10 * scheduler.block_size,
+        common_prefix_len=4 * scheduler.block_size,
+    )
+    scheduler.add_request(newcomer)
+
+    get_local_hit = scheduler._get_local_prefix_cache_hit
+
+    def divergent_local_hit(request):
+        blocks, tokens, boundary, _ = get_local_hit(request)
+        return blocks, tokens, boundary, True

When a rejected KV-load frame reaches the end of prefill and samples a token, `_post_update_kernel` has already incremented `total_len`, written `all_token_ids` and `last_sampled_tokens`, and updated `output_bin_counts`; overlapping async frames can add more such state. This branch restores only `num_computed_tokens`, even though the scheduler now discards those sampled tokens. The recovery token is consequently appended after the stale tokens, so subsequent decoding and sampling penalties use the wrong history. Rebuild or roll back all sampled-token state for rewound requests, not just the computed-token offset.

A downstream data point for whoever picks this up for review.

NVIDIA's vLLM containers currently ship a config-level workaround for this path — we gate `kv_load_failure_policy="recompute"` off entirely, because on the release we ship (v0.27.1-based) the recovery path either crashes the engine (async scheduling) or returns corrupted output (sync scheduling), and every crash-only mitigation we measured just converts the loud failure into a silent one. This PR is what lets us replace that gate with a real fix.

State of the evidence, in case it helps the review start from something concrete:

- The current head (`f2e2abd46`) is **independently verified** against the shipped reproduction: no `num_output_placeholders` assert, and recovered output per-request matches the correct oracle — rejected requests reproduce connector-free recomputation, unaffected requests keep external-reuse output ([details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53298#issuecomment-5442764086)).
- The base commit crashes on the same setup, so the delta is attributable to this PR alone.
- The root cause it fixes on the wrong-output side is traced step-by-step in [#49250](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49250#issuecomment-5430084907).

Nothing here is a request of @Lewis-panda — the PR has already addressed everything we found, quickly. It just seems to be waiting on a maintainer review, and we wanted the review to know a distributor is carrying a workaround against it. Happy to re-run the verification on any revision, or share the harness.
